cues.zh: 它不知道。它只是一段软件。我们会告诉它一个非常有说服力的谎言。这个谎言就是卷管理。卷管理就这样诞生了。我们要做的，就是拿来一堆磁盘，然后让它看起来，嘘，嘘，看起来像一块磁盘。它不知道。所以文件系统就运行在这里，以为自己正愉快地和一块磁盘通信。与此同时，你实际上是在和下面的多块磁盘通信。这样做是有充分理由的。

cues.en: often lies start off with good reasons. And if you can get away with it, maybe that's the end of it. cues.zh: 顺便说一句，另一个重要的现实是，DRAM 的容量其实很大，我们希望能充分利用起来。我们还预见到——好，前两个判断是对的；但这里稍微有点跑偏，他们当时真正针对的设计目标之一，是非易失性主内存的普及。早在 2001 年，我还以为到 2014 年肯定——“你刚从 2014 年穿越回来？哇，非易失性主存怎么样了？”结果对方肯定是一脸“你特么在扯啥？根本没有”。

cues.en: No, it's like you're so pathetic. It's never going to happen. I would love to see non-volume made memory. I don't know if we're going to see it. But the ZFS was also kind of designed with that in mind. So there are these big trends that ZFS was designed around. Blew up the volume management divide. And now you've got one cloud, effectively, where you plug disks into the bottom. And you have file systems plugging in at the top. Because a file system really is only an administrative nexus. It shouldn't be anything more than that.
cues.zh: 不，就好像在说“你太可怜了，根本不可能发生”。虽然我也很想看到非易失性主存，但不知道能不能见到。不过 ZFS 当初也是兼顾了这一点来设计的。ZFS 正是围绕着这些大趋势设计的。它彻底炸平了卷管理的界限。现在你实际上有了一团资源池，底下插磁盘，顶层接入文件系统。因为文件系统本质上只是个管理纽带，本就不该承担更多职责。

cues.en: So you should be able, there should be no real, I mean a file system is just, it is a path, it is hierarchy, and it is policy. That's it. That's all a file system should be. A file system shouldn't have any direct one-to-one association with a disk. Lie or not. So in the ZFS model, you just ZFS create a file system. There's no, you don't have to have a corresponding disk. Similarly, we've got multiple RAID policies, you can have
cues.zh: 所以你本应该……其实文件系统本身就只是：路径、层级结构，还有策略。仅此而已。文件系统本来就该只有这些。文件系统不应该和某块磁盘存在任何直接的一对一对应关系。管它说没说谎。所以在 ZFS 的模型里，你只要 zfs create 一个文件系统就行。没有……你不需要非得有一块对应的磁盘。同样，我们有多种 RAID 策略，你可以用

cues.en: mirroring, Ray-Z2, Delperi-Ray, and so on, and that's been added to over time. And that allows you to solve a whole bunch of manageability problems. And you can deal, because ZFS, one of the great things about it, is because it's a totally copy-on-write design, you don't have an on-disk consistency check. There is no FSCK for ZFS. Such a thing doesn't make sense. ZFS is always consistent on disk. And actually, one of the things that they've kind of interesting is
cues.zh: 镜像、RAID-Z2、双校验 RAID 等等，这些都是后来逐步添加的。这能让你解决一大堆可管理性问题。而且你能应对……因为 ZFS 的一大亮点在于，它是纯写时复制（copy-on-write）设计，所以你不需要做磁盘一致性检查。ZFS 没有 fsck。这种东西根本没有意义。ZFS 在磁盘上永远是一致的。而且实际上，他们做的一个很有意思的事情是，

cues.en: dealing with pathologically lying devices. Because you are only as consistent on disk as ultimately the device tells you you are. And so one of the things that ZFS has added over the years is actually the ability to roll tools back transaction by transaction until you get to one that the disk was actually not lying about. I mean, the disk lies all the time. If the disk is the actual enemy, you actually are fucked. I mean, there's nothing that any body of software can do about it.
cues.zh: 应对病态说谎的设备。因为你磁盘上的一致性，终究取决于设备告诉你的一致性。所以这些年来 ZFS 增加的能力之一，其实就是逐个事务往前回滚，直到回滚到磁盘确实没说谎的那个状态。我是说，磁盘总是在说谎。如果磁盘本身就是敌人，那你可就真完蛋了。我是说，任何软件层面的手段对此都无能为力。

cues.en: But you can at least get those disks that are in that gray area that appear to be enemy action, but sometimes sort of the correct data, say the Western Digital Green Drives. CFS has actually evolved to be able to always be consistent on disk, not require FSCK. Because the thing that they saw is that with data sizes climbing, it's like you can't...
cues.zh: 但你至少可以搞定那些处于灰色地带的磁盘——那些看着像在跟你作对、但有时又能返回正确数据的盘，比如西部数据绿盘。ZFS 演进到现在，已经能始终保证磁盘一致性，不需要 fsck。因为他们意识到，随着数据量不断攀升，你根本不可能……

cues.en: I guess Hacker News did try for the 36 hours that were down. You shouldn't try to FSCK a terabyte. That's not a rational thing to go do because the IO speeds of spindles have not fundamentally changed. IBM RAMAC is a 1200 RPM device. Most spindles today are 7200 RPM devices. You have some 10K, some 15K. Then you've got SSDs, which are their own topic of conversation. But that's amazing to me that you've gone from 1200 RPM to 7200 RPM.
cues.zh: 我想 Hacker News 宕机的那 36 个小时里确实试过。你根本不该去尝试 fsck 几个 TB 的数据。这么做毫无道理，因为机械硬盘的 IO 速度根本没有发生质的飞跃。IBM RAMAC 是一台 1200 RPM 的设备。今天大多数机械盘也就是 7200 RPM。有些是 10K，有些是 15K。然后还有 SSD，那完全是另一个话题了。但让我震惊的是，从 1200 RPM 到 7200 RPM，

cues.en: in 50 years. So the performance is not subjectively different. So a terabyte is a lot more storage than we had in 1956, but actually doing random reads from it is actually not materially faster. It's like 4x faster than it was in 1956. That should be terrifying to you. And what that means is you can't go back and just read all your data to check the consistency of your file system. That should be something that does not exist. It doesn't exist in CFS.
cues.zh: 居然花了 50 年。所以性能并没有主观感知上的质变。虽然 1 个 TB 的容量比 1956 年大得多，但在上面做随机读取其实并没有实质性变快。大概也就比 1956 年快了 4 倍而已。这应该让你感到害怕。这意味着你根本不可能回头把所有数据扫一遍，来检查文件系统的一致性。这种做法本就不该存在。在 ZFS 里也确实不存在。

cues.en: ZFS also, by nature, the fact that it kind of owns the whole stack, ZFS checksums every block, but it checksums every block indirectly, which something you can't do when you've got this volume management file system divide. So it knows when it pulls a block off of the disk, it knows what the checksum for that block is supposed to be, not because the checksum is stored in the block, but because the checksum is stored in the block that points to that block. So it knows when it's got the wrong data.
cues.zh: 从本质上讲，由于 ZFS 掌控了整个存储技术栈，它会对每个数据块做校验，而且是间接校验——在卷管理和文件系统割裂的架构下，这是根本做不到的。因此，当它从磁盘读取一个数据块时，它预先就知道这个块的校验和应该是什么；这并不是因为校验和写在该块内部，而是因为它记录在指向该块的上一级块中。所以，一旦读到错误数据，它立刻就能发现。

cues.en: I'd be like, hey, oh, you firmware, that's the wrong one. I got you. No, no, don't give me that one, asshole. And if you mirror, ZFS will actually heal your data. So ZFS, if you get the wrong data off of one half of the mirror, ZFS will write the good copy over it, and you get these errors. Early in ZFS's life,
cues.zh: 它就好像在说：“嘿固件，你给错数据了，被我逮到了吧，混蛋少拿这个糊弄我。”如果你做了镜像，ZFS 还能真正自愈数据：当从镜像的一侧读到坏数据时，ZFS 会直接用完好的一份覆盖修复它，同时向你报错。在 ZFS 发展的早期，

cues.en: we would see these checksum errors come out of ZFS. And it would say, don't worry, I had some checksum errors, but it's cool, I got the right data. And you're like, okay, that's obviously wrong, because we are running on, and you can pick your vendor, you can pick your controller. We had one where it's like we were getting really persistent checksum errors from every instance of a particular controller.
cues.zh: 我们经常看到 ZFS 抛出这些校验错误。它会提示：“别担心，虽然出了些校验错误，但没关系，我拿到正确数据了。”而你可能会觉得：“好吧，这肯定哪儿搞错了，因为我们跑的可是……”随便哪家大厂、哪款控制器都行。我们曾遇到过一个情况，某款特定控制器的每一个实例都在持续报出校验错误。

cues.en: that was like, there was like six million of these in existence. And you're just like, this controller, I'm sorry, this controller can't be this broken. It's just not possible. As it turns out, it was that broken. And there was a bug, a silicon bug in the DMA engine. And it just like, under certain conditions that were actually relatively reproducible, it just wouldn't DMA the last 64 bytes of a block. Just didn't feel like it.
cues.zh: 而市面上这种控制器大概有六百万个。你当时就会想：“不好意思，这控制器绝不可能烂成这样，根本不可能。”但事实证明，它真就这么烂。它的 DMA 引擎里存在一个芯片级 bug，在某些其实相对容易复现的条件下，它直接就不给数据块的最后 64 字节做 DMA，单纯就是任性不传。

cues.en: And God only knows how many life support systems suddenly clicked off because the last 64 bytes was missing from these payloads. And we would see this across the board. What was great is, and this again happened early in ZFS's life, it's not as amusing now because people now trust ZFS as opposed to whatever they're deployed on. But you get the, no, no, ZFS has to be wrong because I spent so much money on SanX.
cues.zh: 天知道有多少生命维持系统，就因为数据包少了这最后 64 字节而突然停摆。当时我们在各种场景下都屡屡撞见这个问题。最妙的是——这同样发生在 ZFS 早期，现在听起来可能没那么好笑了，因为大家现在信任的是 ZFS，而不是底层跑的那些硬件——但当时大家的第一反应是：“不不不，肯定是 ZFS 错了，我可是在 SanX 上砸了巨资的。”

cues.en: It can't be wrong. It's like, well, funny story, it actually is wrong. And these guys get it wrong. It's because it's hard. It's the reason they get it wrong. But ZFS has been, again, over the years, we've gotten to the point where we've got absolute data reliability. One thing I would say, by the way, and this should be true for any system that is designed around safety and integrity, ZFS never went through an era where it was unsafe or didn't have integrity.
cues.zh: “它绝不可能出错。”但搞笑的是，它还真就出错了。那些厂商确实会搞砸，因为存储本就极度复杂，这就是他们会出错的原因。但这些年走过来，ZFS 已经做到了绝对的数据可靠性。顺便说一句，这也是任何以安全与完整性为核心设计的系统所应具备的底色：ZFS 从未经历过哪怕一段不安全、或是无法保证完整性的时期。

cues.en: or like people lost data. And it's kind of amazing to me how, much in software, people are willing to write off software that does this as kind of pubescence. It's like, yeah, I lost my data, but you know, a million eyeballs, like it's getting better all the time. It's like, no, no, no, this is like a 12-year-old who's stealing cars. Like, this is an issue. This is not like, well, he's only 12. It's like, no, he stole a car.
cues.zh: 或者说，就像人们丢了数据。让我很惊讶的是，在软件领域，人们多愿意把会干这种事的软件当成青春期的小毛病一笔带过。就好像，是啊，我丢了数据，但你知道，有百万双眼睛盯着，它一直在变好。可这不是，不是，不是，这就像一个12岁小孩在偷车。这是个问题。不能说，哎呀他才12岁。不行，他偷了车。

cues.en: at gunpoint having just robbed a liquor store. Like, you've got an issue here. This is not, you can't just be like, well, call me when he's 18. It's like, yeah, you want to see what this guy's like when he's 18? And so this whole idea of like, oh, you know, I have benefits lost my data, but yeah, I'll come back tomorrow. It's like, no, no, no, that's, there are things that are wrong by architecture. And ZFS was architected to be reliable in terms of data. So, and that's kind of the, and we can go into lots and lots of depth on ZFS.
cues.zh: 而且是刚抢完酒类专卖店、持枪偷的。你这就有大问题了。这不是你说“等他18岁再叫我”就行的。是啊，你想看看这家伙18岁时什么样吗？所以那种想法——哦，你知道，我丢了数据，但没事，我明天再来——不行不行，有些东西从架构上就是错的。而 ZFS 的架构目标就是在数据方面可靠。所以，这就是那个……我们可以深入聊很多 ZFS 的细节。

cues.en: In terms of my own personal history, at Sun, we had developed ZFS. In 2006, I and a bunch of coworkers wanted to go and actually build an enterprise storage product around ZFS. So that's what we did. And we regrettably succeeded. And unfortunately, we...
cues.zh: 就我个人的经历来说，在 Sun 时，我们开发了 ZFS。2006年，我和一群同事想真正围绕 ZFS 做一个企业级存储产品。我们就这么做了。遗憾的是，我们成功了。不幸的是，我们……

cues.en: One of our biggest early customers was actually a customer that we hadn't sold a lot of gear to in a long time. This database company you might have heard of. Sadly, I think that there is, at least to a certain degree, they're like, oh wow, you guys are making interesting things again. So we were actually.
cues.zh: 我们早期最大的客户之一，其实是很久没从我们这儿买多少设备的一个客户。就是那家你可能听说过的数据库公司。遗憾的是，我觉得至少在一定程度上，他们的反应是：哇，你们又开始做有意思的东西了。所以我们其实……

cues.en: I think you know, I just I have that daily affirmation. I still feel like I've got survivors guilt. I just feel like there's more I could have done But so we built this storage product based on CFS and Building a storage product by the way, and I say this having gone into this Without what I thought were kind of eyes open in in 2006 and we started doing this building the storage product is like going backpacking in Afghanistan
cues.zh: 我觉得，你知道，我每天都要给自己打气。我仍然有幸存者内疚感。我总觉得我本可以做更多。但我们基于 CFS 做了这个存储产品。顺便说，做存储产品——我这么说，是因为2006年入行时，我自以为已经睁大眼睛了——我们开始做这个存储产品，就像去阿富汗背包旅行。

cues.en: And if you don't think you're going to a war zone, you're delusional. And so we were like, oh, we'll make an enterprise storage product, then it'll be great. And we learned a lot, and we improved ZFS a lot, actually, as a result. The ZFS that you have today is a ZFS that's done a couple of...
cues.zh: 如果你不觉得自己是要去战区，那你就是自欺欺人。于是我们想，哦，我们来做企业级存储产品，那会很棒。结果我们学到了很多，实际上也因此大大改进了 ZFS。你们今天用的 ZFS，是一个经历过几次……

cues.en: gritty tours of duty in the enterprise storage wars because what you learn in doing that is the number of ways that storage can fail. Because going into it, I was like, okay, I got it. Like Phantom Reeds, Phantom Rites, Bitrot, like all good. Sounds good. Oh boy, no, no, no. The firmware is so many steps ahead of you in terms of its creativity and the level of Byzantine failures. Because firmware is like, really, you think that's all I got? We had a firmware bug.
cues.zh: 在企业存储战争里艰苦轮值的 ZFS。因为做这件事会让你学到存储能有多少种失败方式。因为一开始我想，好吧，我懂了。幻读、幻写、位腐烂，都没问题。听起来不错。天哪，不不不。固件在创造力上、在拜占庭故障的程度上，领先你太多步了。因为固件就像：真的吗，你以为我就这点本事？我们遇到过一个固件 bug。

cues.en: This is where I can start rattling off. This is where actually I need to rattle off. My therapist says I need to talk about the firmware revision numbers. Just to let it out, it'll corrode me. So the Seagate SU0D firmware had a beautiful bug in it where they, there was a software bug on the head where it misapplied, the polarity was wrong. On the head, it's like yeah, it's like polarity, head.
cues.zh: 到这里我就可以开始滔滔不绝了。其实这正是我需要一吐为快的地方。我的治疗师说，我得谈谈固件修订号。把它说出来吧，不然会把我腐蚀掉。Seagate SU0D 固件里有个绝妙的 bug：磁头上有软件 bug，把极性搞反了。在磁头上，对，就是极性，磁头。

cues.en: It seems like that's important. It's like, it is important. Yes. And when you got to certain LBAs, got to certain logical block addresses, instead of decelerating the head, it would accelerate the head into the cylinder. And something on the disk, some JTAG or something, was like, oh, no, no, no, you don't mean that. You don't mean that. No, no, no. This will actually, there'll be smoke coming out of it. So it would actually power cycle the device. It would power cycle the drive. And it would bounce the drive. Well, how long did it take the drive?
cues.zh: 这听起来挺重要。确实重要。对。当你访问到某些 LBA、某些逻辑块地址时，它不是让磁头减速，而是让磁头加速撞向柱面。磁盘上的某个东西，某个 JTAG 之类的，就说，哦不不不，你不是这个意思。你不是这个意思。不不不。这真的会冒烟。所以它实际上会让设备断电重启。让驱动器断电重启。然后把驱动器弹回来。那驱动器花了多久

cues.en: to bounce, come back up and start serving IOs. About 650 milliseconds. So you start seeing these IO outliers at 650 milliseconds, you're like, what the fuck is that? And ZFS is not designed at the time, I should say. I think it's the major, major difference between a file system that works that you trust and one that has actually runs hundreds of thousands of spindles in enterprise storage is the ability to sort out these kinds of failures. Because ZFS would go on a long vacation.
cues.zh: 才弹回来、重新上线并开始处理 IO。大约 650 毫秒。于是你开始看到这些 650 毫秒的 IO 离群值，你会想，这他妈是什么？我得说，ZFS 当时不是这么设计的。我认为，一个你信任且能正常工作的文件系统，和一个真正在企业存储里跑过几十万块磁盘的文件系统，最大的区别就在于能不能理清这类故障。因为 ZFS 会去度个长假。

cues.en: when it would hit these kind of spindles. And it would be like, just because the problem is the IO would, because it was effectively a race condition of the head, the IO could succeed. And because the IO could succeed, ZFS would kind of drag on. Well, the whole array would kind of, would grind down. Doing things like big snapshot deletion, doing things like, I mean, if you ever, if you were using ZFS back in the day, if you had a gigantic snapshot and deleted it, we would be doing a bunch of random read from the context of a transaction, which would, the,
cues.zh: 当它碰到这类磁盘时。情况会像这样：问题在于 IO 会……因为本质上这是磁头的竞态条件，IO 可能成功。而正因为 IO 可能成功，ZFS 就会这么拖着。整个阵列就会……慢慢被磨下去。比如做大型快照删除，比如，我是说，如果你当年用过 ZFS，如果你有一个巨大的快照并把它删掉，我们会在一个事务的上下文里做大量随机读，这会……

cues.en: As I said, at FisherWorks, we never lost anyone's data, but it went on some very, very, very long vacations. And it was like, oh, Lassie, come home. Let's see, today, it is Monday. And it literally is gonna be like, by Thursday at 8 p.m., it'll be done.
cues.zh: 就像我说的，在 FisherWorks，我们从没丢过任何人的数据，但它会度一些非常非常非常长的假。就像在喊，哦，Lassie，回家吧。问题是，你可能就在机器上，你能看到，你其实可以用 GTrays 看它的进度，然后你会想，我确实有个客户，就像，好吧，我在算进度，好吧，我知道这什么时候能完成，这个事务组什么时候会同步出去。看看，今天是周一。而它真的会像，到周四晚上 8 点，它就会完成。

cues.en: And he's like, yeah, fortunately, I don't care about the date on the system. So let's just throw this one overboard and start over. But we repaired all those things. cues.en: Write programs that handle text streams because that is a universal interface. So that is, I believe, the most important philosophy in systems development. I think that we should all apply this to everything that we do. The way we are able to develop complicated systems is by building them out of simple ones. Taking simple systems and actually connecting them in interesting and new ways. And the way you're able to do that is by having programs do one thing and they do it well.
cues.zh: 编写处理文本流的程序，因为文本流是一种通用接口。所以我认为，这是系统开发中最重要的哲学。我们都应该把它应用到自己做的每件事上。我们之所以能够开发复杂系统，是因为我们用简单系统来构建它们，把简单系统连接起来，形成有趣而新颖的组合。而要做到这一点，就要让程序只做一件事，并且把它做好。

cues.en: And I think that, by the way, not everyone believes this. There's a bit of attention, I think, between, and the older I get, the more I kind of view it as a holy war, between the forces of complexity and the forces of simplicity. The forces making these big, complicated, for lack of a better word, and I'm sorry if I offend anybody, but I think it is a framework-centric view versus a library-centric view.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我觉得并不是所有人都相信这一点。复杂性的力量和简单性的力量之间存在一种张力，而且我年纪越大，越觉得这有点像一场圣战。复杂性这一方试图构建这些庞大而复杂的东西，恕我直言，也希望不会冒犯任何人，但我认为这是一种以框架为中心的观点，而另一种则是以库为中心的观点。

cues.en: The library-centric view says, hey, I'm going to come up, and I got a bunch of toolboxes for you. Got a bunch of tools. You can use them however you want to use them. The framework's point of view says, OK, you pop into existence in this crazy-ass context.
cues.zh: 以库为中心的观点会说：好，我来给你准备一堆工具箱，里面有很多工具，你想怎么用都可以。以框架为中心的观点则会说：好吧，你会突然出现在这个疯狂的上下文里。
